items.summary: Nvidia lost founding CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned on Nov 12 amid disclosures of relationships with a woman identified as a Chinese spy and an executive reporting to him. Shares fell 14% in five days, though analysts expect little near-term business impact given Nvidia's dominant AI chip position—holding about 90% of the advanced AI chip market—with cash reserves enabling continued investment. The article draws on Silicon Valley succession history: Steve Jobs' return at Apple after John Sculley; Tim Cook and later John Ternus leading Microsoft (valued at US$5.16 trillion, S$6.65 trillion); Andrew Grove's Intel tenure followed by Craig Barrett as fortunes declined; Bill Gates handing CEO to sales-focused Steve Ballmer before Satya Nadella refocused the company toward cloud computing (Microsoft valued at US$3.88 trillion). Experts advise Nvidia's board to choose a technically grounded successor, noting Huang had not fully mapped out Nvidia's future despite his decades of success.
items.title: Nvidia's Leadership Succession After Jensen Huang Resignation

items.summary: The ggml-org team released llama.cpp libraries at version 1.0.0, marking a milestone after 3.5 years of growth (s3). The project runs multi-modal LLMs across hardware from consumer machines to enterprise servers via quantization and portable C/C++ backends (s0-s1). With support for more than 150 architecture variants (s22), the team prioritizes a stable API, stricter versioning boundaries, improved CI infrastructure backed by Hugging Face technologies and contributions from NVIDIA, AMD, Qualcomm, Arm, IBM and Intel (s7-s16).
items.title: llama.cpp v1.0.0 : A stronger foundation for the local AI ecosystem

items.summary: When former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned amid espionage allegations, Singapore-based retail investors rushed to buy the chipmaker's shares. Asiya Bakht, a 52-year-old PR founder, snapped up more stock as prices fell, with her holding now worth five figures. Trading surged across brokers: Syfe saw orders hit about 13 times their daily average, while FSM Global recorded volume at roughly 11 times its October level and IG nearly six times the prior week's. Nvidia shares dropped another 14% on Nov 12, adding to an 11% weekly decline that wiped about US$490 billion (S$630 billion) off market value. Some investors hedged with options; others like banker Joel Tan sold holdings amid leadership uncertainty.
items.title: Singapore Retail Investors Buy Nvidia Dip After Jensen Huang Scandal and Resignation

items.summary: A major global Microsoft outage has disrupted or disabled services including email and AI products, with no cyber-security incident involved; instead Microsoft attributed it to elevated load after many servers became unexpectedly unavailable. Over 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps, though Downdetector recorded only 140,000 reports from 74 countries on Thursday evening, likely undercounting the true scale. Disruption has spread worldwide: OpenAI and Anthropic reported problems, courts in Los Angeles to Texas warned of delays, Toronto hospitals faced email issues without affecting patient care, Japan's shared IT platform was disrupted, and UK GP surgeries, pharmacies, police and schools were impacted. The outage lasted more than 20 hours; experts say the failure snowballs as devices keep trying to reconnect during recovery.
items.title: What we know about the global Microsoft outage

items.summary: At least 74 countries have been affected by a Microsoft 365 outage, which disrupted Teams, Outlook and Copilot since it was detected after midday US Eastern Time on Thursday. The company reported encouraging recovery in Europe while North America also improved. In the US, House staff halted work; OpenAI investigated connection issues; courts warned of delays; Workhorse Group rescheduled its earnings report to 16 November from 12 November. Canadian hospitals, Via Rail and municipalities urged phone contact instead of email. In Japan some firms switched to fax machines while government IT was disrupted. Singapore's courts faced email problems but kept emergency services running. India's equity traders panicked over lost research reports; China users relied on Outlook for international communication despite the Great Firewall. Australia's spy agencies reported minimal impact, mostly affecting email systems.
items.title: How the Microsoft outage has been felt around the world

items.summary: Jensen Huang's resignation from Nvidia has drawn concern in Israel, the company's 'second home.' While Nvidia and other firms like Intel and Microsoft invest heavily there—Nvidia employs 6,000 locals—the leadership crisis may loosen its grip. Investors worry slower decisions could open room for challengers building AI-specific chips and inference software, though uncertainty might also shrink overall spending.
items.title: Israel's VCs See Opportunity for Challengers in Nvidia's Turmoil

items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reports that outgoing NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang called interim CFO Collette Kress "a deer in the headlights," saying she couldn't help steer strategy. She has 13 years at NVIDIA and questioned credit-based deals tied to son-in-law Nico Caprez, scaling back OpenAI's Ohio commitment from $250 billion to $105 billion. Huang resigned Thursday over two reported affairs; a third was later reported by Reuters.
items.title: Jensen Huang's lukewarm view of successor Kress

items.summary: Oracle faces mounting pressure as it winds down a 2023 Microsoft deal to rent AI computing for its Copilot assistant, reportedly because the Nvidia chips powering it were already outdated. This mirrors an earlier $7 billion chip cancellation with Tencent under Trump administration pressure. The moves underscore investor anxieties about AI infrastructure becoming obsolete before recouping costs and mismatched build timelines.
items.title: Microsoft Winding Down Oracle AI Deal Signals Broader Concerns

items.summary: Microsoft warned that its November 2026 security updates can break printing of documents with complex formatting, specifically images rendered at zero height or width. The issue mainly affects Microsoft Word files printed via GDI on Windows Server and client devices running Windows 10 or later.
items.title: Microsoft's November 2026 Updates Break Printing for Complex Documents

items.summary: Dyania Health's Synapsis AI is a clinical reasoning engine that processes patient records within hospital firewalls, using NVIDIA-accelerated computing to surface traceable evidence for clinician review. At Cleveland Clinic, it supported a study of more than 7,800 aortic valve replacement patients between 2005 and 2021, building predictive models of valve deterioration at three-, five- and ten-year intervals.
items.title: AI-Powered Clinical Reasoning Accelerates Patient Care at Dyania Health and Cleveland Clinic

items.summary: Google Cloud released TPU Sync, an open-source Apache-2.0 C++ library that moves key-value (KV) caches and model weights across the memory hierarchy of its TPUs using asynchronous DMA. The tool targets inference bottlenecks in large mixture-of-experts models, reporting over 90% lower KV transfer latency on 235B to 480B parameter MoE models during internal July 2026 tests on TPU v7x (Ironwood). It supports PyTorch via TorchTPU and JAX natively. Google notes all figures are self-reported, early-stage, and not yet recommended for general use.
items.title: Google Releases TPU Sync for Open-Source KV Cache Transfer on TPUs

items.summary: Google DeepMind released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a closed-weights model built for everyday agent loops. It features a 1,048,576-token unified window across input, thinking and output, served via the API only with no self-hosting or quantized variants. Google reports it scores 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at high level—above Gemini 4 Argon's 50—and reaches 57% on Terminal-Bench 4.1 versus 18.2% for Gemini 3.8 Flash. Priced at $1.50/$7.50 per million tokens, it is positioned as a faster daily driver that pairs with Carbon in Antigravity.
items.title: Google Releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen for Coding and Agentic Work

items.summary: European Commission published its long-awaited Digital Fairness Act (DFA), which would replace the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive with a directly applicable Regulation and ban manipulative design. Itxaso Domínguez de Olazábal of European Digital Rights (EDRi) welcomes parts, including a blacklist of ten dark patterns and recognition that using a service can be a commercial decision under Article 17. Yet the law largely relies on opt-outs for addictive features; its impact assessment estimated €13.7 billion in prevented consumer detriment annually. The proposal also narrowed protections for particularly vulnerable consumers to serious misfortune, excluding temporary or situational vulnerabilities. EDRi argues this places burden of proof on regulators and users rather than companies that design systems. It urges the European Parliament and Council to add proportionate obligations requiring traders to assess foreseeable risks before deploying harmful practices.
items.title: The EU Promises Digital Fairness, But Still Wants Users To Do the Work

items.summary: Databricks has made Genie Migrate for Lakehouse generally available. It is an AI coding agent that automates end-to-end migration of SQL from legacy data warehouses to the Databricks Lakehouse as open ANSI SQL, mapping dependencies and converting files in parallel while letting engineers review results. All seven supported sources—Microsoft SQL Server, Azure Synapse, Teradata, Oracle, Snowflake, Amazon Redshift, and Google BigQuery—are now generally available; ETL support is coming soon. On benchmarks the agent converted more than 90% of files correctly for each source. MIXI's MONSTER STRIKE team reported that about 85% of tested BigQuery files ran without manual edits, with the rest needing only one-line fixes.
items.title: Databricks Genie Migrate for Lakehouse Reaches General Availability Across Seven Data Warehouses

items.summary: Miami-based NAED Energy Holding rates its PV-1 PECVD-V vertical in-line deposition platform at 96,000 wafers per hour, double the previous XL-class line. It targets a T2X perovskite/HJT tandem cell aiming for 30% efficiency and glass-glass modules from 600 W. NAED says six of 13 process tools are complete; figures are rated or target values.
items.title: NAED Energy Holding's Vertical Deposition Line for Tandem Solar Cells

items.summary: On Friday, South Korea's Science and ICT Minister Bae Kyung-hoon confirmed that Nvidia will proceed with its pledge to supply 260,000 advanced GPUs. The commitment was reached last year at APEC meetings when Jensen Huang visited the country. It stands despite his resignation as chief executive. Both sides will continue joint projects including linking Korean-made AI chips with Nvidia's platform and building AI infrastructure.
items.title: South Korea Says Nvidia Will Keep GPU Pledges After Huang's Resignation

items.summary: On Friday (Nov 13), China warned the United States against adding export controls on semiconductors amid the Nvidia scandal. Foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said Beijing opposes abusing such measures, which disrupt global supply chains and serve no one's interests, urging continued cooperation under existing US-China consensus. The controversy stems from co-founder Jensen Huang's resignation over an affair with Alice Huang of Singapore-based Megaspeed, a company reportedly suspected by the Commerce Department—under Secretary Howard Lutnick—of rerouting restricted Nvidia technology to China.
items.title: China Warns Against New US Chip Export Controls After Nvidia Scandal

items.summary: Filings list servers worth 485 million yuan ($73 million) as collateral, including units with restricted Nvidia chips. Megaspeed, which Alice Huang founded in 2023, is under investigation for allegedly illegally shipping Nvidia chips into China and has denied the allegations. The hardware included 52 Super Micro Computer servers fitted with H100 or H200 processors from Nvidia.
items.title: Documents Tie Banned Nvidia AI Chips to Alice Huang-Linked Shanghai Data Center

items.summary: The International Energy Agency reports the world's oil supply has swung back into surplus for the first time since the start of the US-Israeli war against Iran, with October supplies outstripping demand by nearly 2m barrels a day as Gulf exports recovered faster than global demand. After months of Hormuz-blocked shipments and Brent crude spiking from $72 to $126 before falling toward $95, the IEA now forecasts supply averaging 105m barrels daily in Q4—1.7m above forecast demand—and expects members to release emergency stockpiles adding another 71m barrels by late February.
items.title: IEA Reports Global Oil Supply Returns to Surplus After Iran War Disruptions

items.summary: Nvidia's chief executive Jensen Huang had unusually close access to President Donald Trump, having joined him on trips and been briefed directly. His reported affair with Alice Huang—a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed—has raised suspicions that Chinese intelligence was targeting someone near the president. US officials suspect links between Huang and Beijing; China denies them. The controversy centers on Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who reportedly resisted acting against Megaspeed despite a classified memo warning of risks, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pushed for action. Nvidia intervened in an investigation into suspected chip smuggling. Members of Congress from both parties are demanding answers as pressure mounts.
items.title: How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House

items.summary: In a Politics Weekly America podcast, Jonathan Freedland speaks with New Yorker's Susan Glasser about why Donald Trump's judgment of high-profile men appears questionable. The discussion centers on how the Nvidia cheating scandal complicates Trump's handling of prominent figures and his own credibility.
items.title: Why the Nvidia cheating scandal is bad for Trump

items.summary: For India's emerging neocloud providers—Yotta, E2E Networks and Neysa—access to computing power is the business. These specialized cloud operators let enterprises, startups and research institutions rent high-performance GPUs rather than invest in their own infrastructure, positioning them as an important layer in India's AI ecosystem. Yet this boom rests on heavy dependence on a single company: NVIDIA—which now faces leadership turmoil and supply-chain risks.
items.title: India's AI infrastructure bet hinges on NVIDIA amid leadership crisis and supply-chain risks

items.summary: Nvidia lacked a succession plan for ousted founder-CEO Jensen Huang, though it had attempted to hire an external number two before his departure. Candidates avoided working in his shadow; one Slack group titled 'Stand with Jensen' exists, and few fewer than 10 people worldwide are seen as capable of running the company. The successor must keep Nvidia's products shipping on time while sustaining the entire industry—no replacement is readily available.
items.title: Nvidia's Next CEO Must Keep an Entire Industry Alive

items.summary: CoreWeave, whose stock has been volatile on the Nvidia saga, is pursuing a $4 billion loan syndicated by Morgan Stanley and Mitsubishi UFJ. The debt will be collateralized by contracts with Meta, allowing CoreWeave to benefit from Meta's strong credit standing. Early marketing reception was positive, with an all-in interest rate around 7.5%, far cheaper than the nearly 16% yield its unsecured bonds have hit.
items.title: CoreWeave Secures $4B Loan Backed by Meta Contracts Amid Nvidia Uncertainty

items.summary: Singapore-based investor Leo Chengwon Kohan, who has invested roughly $1.3 billion in Nvidia and holds a net worth of about $13.2 billion per the Bloomberg Billionaires Index, refused to add further capital after former CEO Jensen Huang's removal over alleged affairs and espionage suspicions. Kohan demanded Huang's reinstatement as 'supreme creator' of AI and superintelligence chips, citing support from Elon Musk, Gavin Becker and President Trump; he plans reduced Nvidia investment while funding other superintelligence firms.
items.title: Nvidia Investor Leo Chengwon Kohan Halts Further Investment Over Jensen Huang Ouster

items.summary: A field experiment in 43 Indian garment factories run by Shahi Exports tested whether an anonymous worker-voice tool, Inache (by Good Business Lab), raised productivity. Randomly assigned in 2019 into three groups—tool only, tool plus HR incentives, and control—the study found no significant effects for the tool alone, but meaningful gains where human-resources teams had measurable response targets tied to rewards. Absenteeism fell by -12.7% (about one percentage point against a 7.9% mean), monthly earnings rose +3.2%, and productivity increased +4.7% (against a 53% control mean). Turnover may have dropped (-6%), though that estimate is imprecise due to pandemic disruption. Gains came through faster, higher-quality HR responses and more grievances raised—830 total over the period—with production-related reports driving output gains by enabling fixes like fan repairs in heat.
items.title: Worker Voice Tools Raise Productivity Only With Aligned HR Incentives

items.summary: A Microsoft Outlook email outage left millions of individuals, organizations and businesses without access on Thursday, including NPR's newsroom. Down for more than 12 hours, the service reported only marginal success early Friday, attributing it to elevated load rather than malicious activity. Teams and Copilot were also affected across more than 70 countries.
items.title: Microsoft scrambles to fix email outage

items.summary: A worldwide outage of critical Microsoft systems disrupted businesses and public services, affecting millions for over 12 hours before the company reported early signs of stabilisation. More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps, with more than 90% of Fortune 500 companies relying on its Copilot AI chatbot; no cyber-attack was indicated as a cause.
items.title: Global Microsoft Outage and Other Top Stories

items.summary: Nvidia announced that CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down after admitting to extramarital affairs, including one with a client allegedly recruited by China's top spy agency. CFO Colette Kress becomes interim CEO during the AI-chip crisis. The scandal raises questions at the White House and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick about chip export restrictions. Separately, Sen. Chris Van Hollen will challenge Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader, citing voter desire for change.
items.title: Nvidia CEO steps down. And, Sen. Chris Van Hollen to run for majority leader

items.summary: Following Jensen Huang's resignation amid a personal scandal, Nvidia lost about $1.8tn (€1.6tn) in market value since its October 6 record close of $239.24 per share. Colette Kress now leads as interim CEO while the board seeks a permanent successor. Analysts debate whether investors will accept continued dealmaking pace and how much growth remains if customers slow AI spending. Price targets have fallen sharply, with Yorkville Ives at $225 (down 25% from $300), Bernstein and Baird at $200, Citi at $225, and Goldman Sachs holding a buy rating at $220.
items.title: Nvidia’s $1.8tn Value Drop After Jensen Huang Departure

items.summary: 2026 began with Wall Street's trillion-dollar AI bet paying off, but a second-half sell-off—triggered by midterm results and Nvidia turmoil over alleged ties to a suspected Chinese spy—erased more than $1 trillion from the Magnificent Seven in one day. Analysts dispute whether this signals a bursting bubble or merely a healthy correction amid roughly $800 billion of 2026 capex, with further spending planned through 2028.
items.title: Is the AI Bubble Bursting as Anthropic Goes Public?

items.summary: This article explores the environmental and economic costs of dependence on a few large technology companies, using cloud computing as its central example. It notes that data centres consumed 415 terawatt-hours in 2024 (about 1.5% of global demand), projected to reach 945 terawatt-hours by 2030 largely due to AI. Microsoft reported a 25% rise in total emissions in 2025, driven by expanding data centres and accounting changes. The piece links software lock-in—exemplified by Windows 10 support ending in October 2025—to reduced consumer choice over greener alternatives, and cites global e-waste of 62 million metric tonnes (only 22.3% formally recycled) plus US$78 billion (£59 billion) in externalised costs in 2022. It calls for procurement decisions based on lifetime cost, lifespan and emissions rather than the next annual bill.
items.title: The Costs of Digital Dependence on Microsoft and Cloud Technology

items.summary: A global Microsoft outage since Thursday afternoon has disrupted Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other services across Portugal. The Ministry of Health's Shared Services confirmed affected bodies are working to restore access, while government ministers reportedly lost email but continued using an unaffected internal network plus WhatsApp and Signal. Schools face communication breakdowns between parents, teachers and pupils. Microsoft attributes the issue to a configuration update causing server overload, rules out cyberattack, and offers no restoration timeframe.
items.title: Global Microsoft Outage Disrupts Portugal Government, Schools and Health Services

items.summary: The global Microsoft 365 outage on Nov 13 disrupted Outlook, Teams and Copilot for more than half a day, spilling into Asia-Pacific business hours. Singapore saw government systems and several banks' email affected, while emergency services and Singpass stayed operational. Experts frame this as an 'over-reliance' problem: efficiency gains from consolidating with major cloud vendors create single points of failure that can cascade across industries. NTU's Boh Wai Fong calls it a 'paradox of digital transformation.' Anupam Chattopadhyay warns the massive complexity makes failures hard to isolate and repair, risking cascading effects. Liu Yang stresses redundancy does not guarantee resilience when services share infrastructure. Choo notes impacts extend beyond email into core business processes, with AI amplifying future risks.
items.title: What the Microsoft Outlook outage reveals about risks, limitations and gaps in communication

items.summary: The removal of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia, the company he led for 33 years, has sent shockwaves through global tech. Nvidia supplies 90% of chips used in data centre servers where sophisticated AI models are trained. The scandal emerged amid a race between major powers to gain supremacy in transformative technology. Allegations that Huang had an affair with a businesswoman reportedly linked to the Chinese government raised national security concerns, prompting bipartisan demands for explanations from Trump and Huang. Lawmakers including Senator John Thune and Representatives Brian Mast and John Moolenaar pushed for testimony or subpoenas. Senators Elizabeth Warren and others insist his resignation does not absolve him of responsibility.
items.title: Congress Demands Answers Over Nvidia Espionage Allegations and Jensen Huang Scandal

items.summary: Reuters obtained an internal Amazon document describing 'World Product Graph,' a plan to aggregate product information on virtually every item sold worldwide, whether or not Amazon stocks it. The initiative aims to make Amazon the definitive shopping destination, reduce reliance on Google for research, fend off Walmart's e-commerce growth, and counter AI shopping agents like Meta's Muse (over 10 million users) that direct traffic elsewhere. A related search agent, Rufus ('Alexa for Shopping'), reportedly gives inaccurate answers despite claims of ~97% accuracy globally; Amazon says usage figures are outdated. The project falls under VP Robert Tekiela and may involve brands such as Coca-Cola, Bayer, and Procter & Gamble contributing data or Amazon crawling retailer sites.
items.title: Exclusive-Amazon’s plan to own the world’s product data and fight AI shopping agents

items.summary: A major global outage at Microsoft disrupted email and cloud-based services across the world on Thursday, affecting businesses, government agencies and public services in 74 countries and territories. The disruption began Thursday and continued into Friday, hitting Microsoft 365 — including Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive and Copilot — with Exchange Online at its core. Downdetector received reports from users in 74 countries within about an hour, with Outlook problems peaking around 130,000 in the US. Microsoft said servers unexpectedly stopped working, then failed again under returning traffic, while reversing a recent network configuration change; executive vice president Charles Lamanna noted no sign of a cyberattack. Impacts were widespread: governments and courts resorted to paper or phone calls, banks confirmed transactions by fax, healthcare facilities reverted to paper prescriptions, airlines reported customer-support disruptions, and companies like Workhorse postponed events.
items.title: Global Microsoft Outage Disrupted Services Worldwide

items.summary: Megaspeed International is the company linked to Nvidia chief Jensen Huang's resignation over alleged extramarital affairs with an accused Chinese spy, Alice Huang. US agencies believe Huang acted as a Chinese intelligence asset passing commercial information to Beijing; China flatly rejects these claims. Megaspeed's global facades are puzzling: near-empty offices in Singapore and Kuala Lumpur, a dilapidated storefront in Malaysia, and no physical presence for its Australian subsidiary on the 10th floor of a Sydney building. Despite purchasing nearly $5bn in Nvidia chips over three years, representatives know nothing about it. Alice Huang was barred from re-entering Singapore and Taiwan; Kai Kang remains unaccounted for. Analysts warn Megaspeed could be a front for Chinese intelligence or simply make the parent look credible.
items.title: The baffling corporate trail of Megaspeed International amid Jensen Huang's downfall

items.summary: A major Microsoft outage attributed to elevated load on its infrastructure disrupted email, Teams and Copilot globally within an hour, affecting users in 74 countries and territories across the Americas, Europe, Asia and Africa. Microsoft confirmed repair efforts were not proceeding as expected and was pursuing alternate workstreams to increase capacity, without stating when full service would be restored.
items.title: Microsoft Outlook Outage Disrupts Users Across 74 Countries

items.summary: U.S. lawmakers on Thursday demanded clarity about what President Donald Trump knew regarding Nvidia chief Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, after the AI chipmaker announced his departure. Huang had advocated looser rules on U.S. chip sales to China amid intensifying scrutiny ahead of Trump’s visit.
items.title: Congress Presses Trump and Nvidia Over Jensen Huang’s Exit

items.summary: A major global outage brought Microsoft's widely used tools—including email and cloud storage—to a standstill, with around 130,000 people reporting Outlook access issues by early Thursday afternoon US Eastern time. The company said it was aggressively pursuing pathways to reduce impact while restarting affected servers. Impacts extended well beyond missed emails: family violence workers could not access client databases, schools lost remote lessons, psychologists lost telehealth capacity, businesses stalled on orders, and some government service centres closed. OpenAI and Anthropic also reported problems with their Microsoft 365 connections. The likely cause was a fault in the automated health-check machinery that withdraws servers it deems unwell, leaving healthy ones overwhelmed—an inference rather than a confirmed root cause.
items.title: Microsoft has suffered a global outage. A tech expert explains what went wrong

items.summary: Commentator Wang Yichen argues that right-wing forces in Japan are repackaging militarist symbols as entertainment to normalize them among young people. Evidence includes a rising sun flag banned then reinstated at an Asian Games venue, its appearance at a World Cup match, and controversial depictions of war crimes in anime, manga, films, and military emblems. The author contends that culture is not apolitical; rather, symbols retain their history regardless of context, as seen with Nazi insignia in Europe. This cultural infiltration prepares the social ground for Japan's neo-militarism by shaping a generation unfamiliar with war crimes through softened textbooks and screens.
items.title: Cultural Infiltration Paving the Way for Japan's Neo-Militarism

items.summary: The 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, held November 18-19 at the Shenzhen International Exchange Center in Guangdong Province, will run entirely on green electricity. China Southern Power Grid (CSG) said preparations are complete and it secured 89 million kilowatt-hours of green power to cover all event energy use. Supply comes from offshore wind farms in Yangjiang plus wind and solar bases in northwest China's deserts, Gobi areas and barren lands, transmitted over long-distance interprovincial networks.
items.title: 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting Powered Entirely by Green Electricity

items.summary: As China prepares to host APEC 2026 in Shenzhen, an article argues that regional cooperation benefits economies well beyond the Asia-Pacific. Using Xi Jinping's 2014 'geese flying together' metaphor for the 21-member bloc, it stresses shared prosperity as a foundation for trade. In 2024, these economies accounted for 61% of global GDP and 46% of world goods and services trade. China's growth—GDP doubling from roughly $9.59 trillion in 2014 to about $14 trillion by 2025—and rising imports have boosted Southeast Asian exporters through streamlined e-commerce certificate exchanges with Malaysia, while the Port of Chancay has cut shipping times for Peruvian and Ecuadorian produce to Shanghai. The piece contends that larger economies open markets and finance infrastructure, enabling smaller partners to win customers and sustain trade.
items.title: How Asia-Pacific Cooperation Is Shaping the Global Economy

items.summary: As the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting prepares in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province, digital infrastructure has become central to inclusive Asia-Pacific cooperation. Experts discuss easing computing-power and energy bottlenecks, responsible tech investment, and pragmatic guidance for participants: economies need not build foundation models from scratch but can adapt mature AI solutions to local industrial and agricultural needs.
items.title: Digital Silk Road: Bytes and a Shared Future for APEC

items.summary: A World Weather Attribution rapid analysis found human-caused climate change amplified extreme heat during Indonesia's 2026 fire season, turning an El Niño-driven drought into a severe regional crisis. Fires burned about 1.9 million hectares of peatland and rainforest in western Indonesia between August and October 2026.
items.title: Climate Change Intensified Indonesia's 2026 Fire Crisis

items.summary: An alleged illegal surveillance operation targeting President Prabowo Subianto and other senior figures has exposed deep tensions in Indonesia's security establishment. Former police chief Listyo Sigit Prabowo was among four officers named as suspects; investigators say communications were intercepted without authorization across 2025-2026 before records were deleted. The new police chief, Suyudi Ario Seto, confirmed the operation targeted a broad range of officials and activists. Amnesty International called for investigations into whether critics were intimidated. Analysts trace widespread surveillance to Suharto-era practices that persist today, with no effective regulation constraining law enforcement. The scandal intensifies friction between Prabowo and predecessor Joko Widodo amid ongoing leadership turmoil.
items.title: Indonesia's Wiretapping Scandal Opens a Political Fault Line

items.summary: Bloomberg reported that Aperia Cloud Services, an official Nvidia partner in Singapore, purchased servers containing banned H800 chips from Dell Technologies; those servers later reached Shanghai Longteng Intelligent Computing. The U.S. had barred H800 exports to China in 2023 amid concerns about circumvention of restrictions aimed at slowing Beijing's AI development.
items.title: Chinese Firm Linked to Alice Huang Acquired Banned Nvidia Chips

items.summary: A Microsoft outage lasting nearly 18 hours disrupted Outlook, Teams and Copilot worldwide from Thursday to Friday, drawing about 200,000 user reports. The failure affected AI firms OpenAI and Anthropic through their Microsoft 365 connectors, aviation via SpiceJet flight cancellations in India, and IT services broadly. Experts note that even a few hours of disruption can ripple into reduced output across the day, with severity varying by project. Unlike prior outages lasting only a few hours, this event underscored how organizations rely on single digital ecosystems for core operations like approvals and communication.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Exposes Dependence on Single Digital Ecosystem

items.summary: On Tata Motors' Q2 FY27 earnings call, MD-CEO Shailesh Chandra said absolute volumes would stay strong but cost pressures persisted into the third quarter. Passenger Vehicles posted a Rs 5,531 crore loss versus Rs 76,170 crore profit last year, though consolidated revenue rose to Rs 96,920 crore from Rs 72,349 crore. The company offset about 40% of commodity cost impact and expects Q4 relief via price hikes and cost cuts.
items.title: Tata Motors Q3 Cost Pressure and JLR China Uncertainty

items.summary: Nvidia's stock fell more than 13% at Thursday's open after reports that its board was preparing to remove co-founder Jensen Huang, whose 33-year tenure ended in resignation. The departure followed an independent investigation into spying allegations tied to foreign intelligence efforts, alongside revelations of personal misconduct and a reported relationship with colleague Kimberly Powell. Huang held only about 3.6% of Nvidia through family trusts and direct holdings, without super-voting shares, so the board retained decision-making authority. Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while searching for a permanent replacement.
items.title: Jensen Huang Exits Nvidia as CEO Amid Spying Allegations and Leadership Uncertainty

items.summary: The fallout from allegations that Nvidia chief Jensen Huang was entangled with Alice Huang, suspected of Chinese intelligence links, has reframed a corporate scandal as a national-security concern. Former CIA and FBI officials warn honey traps—using intimacy to compromise targets—are an enduring vulnerability harder than firewalls or passwords to defend against. The affair exposes China's layered machinery: the Ministry of State Security, once cautious with its "thousand grains of sand" approach but more aggressive after 2005; military intelligence units including a former PLA department estimated at over 100,000 personnel; and cyber operations tracing to lessons from the Gulf War. Investigations by Congress, the FBI and Nvidia's board remain unfinished, with no public proof Alice Huang was an operative. The case underscores that foreign services increasingly target AI, quantum computing and biotechnology—and that breaches may begin not with sophisticated hacking but ordinary human connections.
items.title: Nvidia Scandal as a Window Into China's Broader Espionage Machine

items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized Nvidia and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick for weak controls over chip exports, citing significant leakage in the system. The remarks followed reports that Jensen Huang had affairs with Alice Huang, a Chinese spy suspect, prompting his resignation as CEO. Colette Kress will serve as interim leader while the board searches for a permanent successor.
items.title: Bessent Criticizes Nvidia and Lutnick Over Chip Export Controls Amid Huang Scandal

items.summary: An evening news roundup covers a Microsoft 365 outage lasting over 16 hours, with gradual but incomplete service restoration. At least 23 people died when a mini-bus collided with a truck near Kaziranga in Assam. Rahul Gandhi accused the Modi government of phone surveillance; Nvidia fell up to 14%, dropping below $4 trillion market value; cash-strapped SpiceJet called an emergency board meeting.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Recovery; Kaziranga Crash Kills 23; Nvidia Slump and Other Business Stories

items.summary: Computer scientist and podcaster Lex Fridman has publicly backed Jensen Huang after his exit from Nvidia, calling the departure a 'huge mistake for America and humanity' and likening it to Apple firing Steve Jobs in 1985. Huang resigned unconditionally late Wednesday amid reports of two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China. Colette Kress was appointed interim CEO, while director Harvey Jones, 73, became the board's first-ever chair. Fridman defended Huang as an extremely proud American and described him as kind, humble, and caring, noting that more than 1,000 close associates praised his character privately.
items.title: Podcaster Lex Fridman Defends Jensen Huang's Ouster From Nvidia

items.summary: On Friday, Microsoft reported completing recovery actions across parts of its affected Asia Pacific infrastructure as traffic gradually restored, though Microsoft 365 services including Outlook remained disrupted for a second day. Mailbox access improved while some users faced intermittent issues; the focus shifted to extending recovery elsewhere and reducing email backlogs.
items.title: Microsoft Asia Pacific Outage Recovery and Outlook Disruption Continue

items.summary: A 2024 photo of Akshay Kumar joking with NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang has resurfaced as meme material following Huang's resignation amid a personal scandal. Users recast the image sarcastically and in Bollywood film scenes, while attention shifted to Indian-origin board member Aarti Shah, who joined Nvidia's Audit and Compensation Committees in 2020 after nearly three decades at Eli Lilly.
items.title: Akshay Kumar's Nvidia Compliment Becomes Meme After Jensen Huang Resignation

items.summary: One 97 Communications said its subsidiary Paytm Payments Services Ltd received in-principle authorisation from the Reserve Bank of India on November 13, 2026 to operate prepaid payment instruments through a letter dated that day. The approval is subject to RBI Master Directions and requires system and cyber security audits by qualified auditors before PPSL can issue wallets; final issuance needs separate certificate authorisation. Paytm reported over 10-fold profit growth to Rs 225 crore, operating revenue up 28% YoY to Rs 2,648 crore, and record Ebitda of Rs 270 crore in Q2 ended September 2026.
items.title: Paytm's PPSL Gets RBI In-Principle Approval for Wallet Operations Amid Strong Q2 Growth

items.summary: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles swung to a consolidated net loss of Rs 5,531 crore in the July–September quarter of FY27, down from a profit of Rs 76,170 crore a year earlier. A Rs 6,738 crore exceptional charge drove the loss and exceeded it by Rs 1,207 crore. Consolidated revenue rose 34 percent to Rs 96,920 crore as domestic momentum continued while JLR restructured.
items.title: Tata Motors PV Posts Q2 FY27 Loss Amid JLR Restructuring

items.summary: A global Microsoft outage disrupted Outlook, Teams and Copilot on Thursday, affecting millions of users across at least 74 countries with roughly 140,000 reports. Aviation was hit in India: IndiGo's email support is affected while Air India rerouted traffic but reported no flight disruption. Governments, financial markets and AI firms OpenAI and Anthropic also faced issues.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Disrupts Outlook, Teams Globally; Indian Airlines Affected

items.summary: A widespread Microsoft outage disrupted access to Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 services worldwide, including India. Nearly 1.3 lakh users reported problems accessing Outlook shortly after 1 pm Eastern Time on Friday (November 13). While reports later declined, users continued facing email and inbox issues. Microsoft attributed the outage to servers unexpectedly failing health checks before becoming unavailable, with recovery attempts not working as expected; no cyberattack was indicated.
items.title: Widespread Microsoft Outage Disrupts Outlook, Teams and Copilot Globally

items.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs reiterated New Delhi's firm diplomatic posture toward Pakistan during a bi-weekly briefing, with spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stressing that political clearances follow national policy. This follows Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann seeking clearance to attend the 4th International World Punjabi Conference in Lahore (November 27-29), where he was invited as chief guest. Mann also called for reopening the suspended Kartarpur Corridor amid strained India-Pakistan relations.
items.title: MEA Reaffirms India's Stance as Punjab CM Seeks Clearance for Lahore Visit

items.summary: Government data released Friday showed India's total exports rose 29.9% to USD 89.99 billion in October, up from USD 69.27 billion a year earlier. Total imports climbed to USD 110.07 billion from USD 94.42 billion. The trade deficit narrowed to USD 20.09 billion from USD 25.15 billion in the same month last year, per PTI reporting for Hindustan Times.
items.title: India's October Exports Jumped Nearly 30% as Trade Deficit Narrowed

items.summary: Nearly three years after the October 2023 glacial lake outburst flood on the Teesta river breached South Lhonak Lake and displaced roughly 80,000 people, families remain stranded in makeshift relief camps across Kalimpong, West Bengal. While Sikkim declared a disaster and sanctioned 4,100 houses plus ₹67.05 lakhs in rental aid to 447 people, West Bengal never classified the flood as such, leaving survivors without housing or support and fearing eviction from forest land. Repeated damage surveys have yet to yield relief: only 116 planned homes await state finance sanction. The riverbed reportedly rose six to 14 metres, with consecutive floods in 2024 and 2025 worsening vulnerability. Experts warn that flood mitigation must occur during the dry season—a window lost through delayed action—while political friction between the GTA and BJP has further stalled governance.
items.title: Three Years After Teesta's GLOF, Survivors Remain in Limbo as the River Closes In
